title: Operadic extension and the relative free-algebra adjunction
statement: Use the operads and algebras of [lem-coef-operadic-algebra-presentability], and let $\mathcal V$ be presentably monoidal. For any map $u:\mathcal M\to\mathcal N$ of small generalized nonsymmetric infinity operads which is an equivalence over $[0]$, with both zero-fibers spaces, restriction $u^*:\operatorname{Alg}_{\mathcal N}(\mathcal V)\to\operatorname{Alg}_{\mathcal M}(\mathcal V)$ has a left adjoint $u_!$. Its unit induces natural equivalences of mapping spaces $\operatorname{Map}(u_!B,C)\simeq\operatorname{Map}(B,u^*C)$. For an ordinary nonsymmetric operad $\mathcal O$, let $\mathcal O_{\mathrm{triv}}$ be its inert part, with the same colors and only inert structure, and let $\tau_{\mathcal O}:\mathcal O_{\mathrm{triv}}\to\mathcal O$ be the inclusion. There is a natural equivalence $\operatorname{Alg}_{\mathcal O_{\mathrm{triv}}}(\mathcal V)\simeq\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal O_{[1]},\mathcal V)$. Let $\operatorname{Alg}_{\mathrm{triv}}(\mathcal V)$ denote the total Cartesian fibration over operads with these trivial-algebra fibers and restriction transports. As $\mathcal O$ varies, restriction $\tau^*:\operatorname{Alg}(\mathcal V)\to\operatorname{Alg}_{\mathrm{triv}}(\mathcal V)$ has a left adjoint relative to the base $\operatorname{Opd}^{\mathrm{ns}}_\infty$. Explicitly, the free functor leaves the base operad fixed, and for any $g:\mathcal O\to\mathcal P$ its mapping-space adjunction restricts to $\operatorname{Map}_{/g}(\tau_{\mathcal O,!}B,C)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{/g}(B,\tau_{\mathcal P}^*C)$, naturally in $g$, including all higher homotopies.

source.place: Theorem A.4.6 and Proposition A.4.3; Proposition 3.4.5 and Lemma 3.6.7 (relative free adjunction). No Stacks tag states this infinity-categorical result.

proof.text: Fix an $\mathcal M$-algebra $B$. Apply [lem-coef-operadic-free-cocone-characterization] with $\mathcal C=\mathcal M$, $\mathcal D=\mathcal N$ and $X=B$. Its hypotheses hold: an operad map preserves inert arrows, $u$ is an equivalence on the two space zero-fibers, both operads are small, and $\mathcal V$ is presentably monoidal. The cited existence clause gives an $\mathcal N$-algebra $D_B$ and $\eta_B:B\to u^*D_B$ whose active-slice cocones are operadically colimiting. Its universal-property clause then gives, naturally for every $\mathcal N$-algebra $C$, the equivalence $\operatorname{Map}(D_B,C)\simeq\operatorname{Map}(B,u^*C)$ induced by composition with $\eta_B$. Thus the covariant mapping-space functor $C\mapsto\operatorname{Map}(B,u^*C)$ is represented by $D_B$. The dual clause of [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-adjoint-criterion], applied to $i=u^*$, assembles these representing objects into the coherent functor $u_!$, with the universal maps $\eta_B$ as unit and the asserted mapping-space bifunctor equivalence. This proves the first clause including higher naturality. The free-cocone theorem includes empty tuples, and no nonempty-color or nonempty-slice assumption was introduced.

proof.text: For the nongeneralized operad $\mathcal O$, the Segal identifications of [lem-coef-operadic-algebra-presentability] give $\mathcal O_{[n]}\simeq\mathcal O_{[1]}^n$ and $\mathcal O_{[0]}\simeq *$. First check that its inert part is again an operad, so its inclusion is eligible for step 1. Form $\mathcal O_{\mathrm{triv}}=\mathcal O\times_{\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}}\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}_{\mathrm{inert}}$, viewed over $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$. Inner horns fill in this subcategory: all their edges, including the composite edge of a two-dimensional inner horn, lie over inert arrows, since inert arrows are closed under composition. The inert lifts and all the fibers are unchanged. By [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion], their cocartesian mapping-space condition restricts to this subcategory: if $\rho$ is inert, $\psi\rho$ is inert exactly when $\psi$ is inert, so the omitted noninert mapping fibers on both sides are empty. The Segal product condition over an inert $\phi$ is unchanged; over a noninert $\phi:[m]\to[n]$ its left side is empty and at least one $\rho_i\phi$ is noninert, since all increments of $\phi^{\mathrm{op}}$ are one exactly when $\phi$ is inert. Thus its right side is empty as well. For $n=0$ every map $[m]\to[0]$ is inert and the unchanged empty-product axiom applies. Hence the operad axioms in [lem-coef-operadic-algebra-presentability] hold, and the inclusion preserves inert lifts and is the identity over $[0]$. Both $\mathcal O$ and $\mathcal O_{\mathrm{triv}}$ are moreover generalized nonsymmetric infinity operads in the sense of [lem-coef-operadic-algebra-presentability], as step 1 requires. Axiom (i) is the same. For (ii), $\mathcal O_{[0]}$ is a contractible Kan complex (shown below), so the iterated homotopy fiber product $\mathcal O_{[1]}\times_{\mathcal O_{[0]}}\cdots\times_{\mathcal O_{[0]}}\mathcal O_{[1]}$ is equivalent to $\mathcal O_{[1]}^n$ compatibly with the Segal map. For (iii), the objects of $I_n$ over $[0]$ are the $n+1$ vertex maps, and for each of them the target $C_\alpha$ lies in $\mathcal O_{[0]}$, so the $n=0$ case of the mapping-space axiom makes every $\operatorname{Map}^{\alpha\phi}(X,C_\alpha)$ contractible. The limit over the zigzag $I_n$, whose $[0]$-terms are contractible, is the iterated homotopy fiber product over points, that is, $\prod_i\operatorname{Map}^{\rho_i\phi}(X,C_i)$; so (iii) is the product axiom already checked. For $n=0$, $I_0$ is the single object $\mathrm{id}_{[0]}$ and (iii) is the empty-product axiom. To check explicitly the space hypothesis of step 1, the equivalence $\mathcal O_{[0]}\simeq *$ makes every edge of $\mathcal O_{[0]}$ an equivalence: a quasi-inverse and its natural equivalence with the identity identify that edge with an identity up to equivalences of its endpoints. Thus $\mathcal O_{[0]}$ equals its core. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-core-kan-fibration] to its projection to the point, which is an isofibration since it is inner and identity equivalences lift degenerately. Its core, and hence the unchanged zero-fiber of both operads, is a Kan complex.

source.place: Definition 3.4.1; verification of the inert suboperad axioms.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-inert-operad-color-reconstruction] with $\mathcal M=\mathcal O$ and the presentably monoidal $\mathcal V$, which is in particular a monoidal infinity category. Its hypotheses hold: $\mathcal O$ is small, and step 2 shows that it is a generalized nonsymmetric infinity operad, in the sense of [lem-coef-operadic-algebra-presentability] whose axioms (i)–(iii) the cited statement repeats, with Kan zero-fiber $\mathcal O_{[0]}$. Its $\mathcal M_{\mathrm{triv}}=\mathcal M\times_{\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}}\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}_{\mathrm{inert}}$ and inclusion $\tau$ are exactly $\mathcal O_{\mathrm{triv}}$ and $\tau_{\mathcal O}$ of step 2, and its algebra category is the full subcategory of inert-preserving functors over $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$, the same as in [lem-coef-operadic-algebra-presentability]. The cited theorem says that restriction to the fiber over $[1]$ is an equivalence $E_{\mathcal O}:\operatorname{Alg}_{\mathcal O_{\mathrm{triv}}}(\mathcal V)\simeq\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal O_{[1]},\mathcal V)$ of infinity categories, including coherent transformations and all higher simplices, with no colimit hypothesis on $\mathcal V$; the empty color category is included. Naturality in $\mathcal O$: an operad map $g:\mathcal O\to\mathcal P$ preserves inert edges and lies over $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$, so it restricts to $g_{\mathrm{triv}}:\mathcal O_{\mathrm{triv}}\to\mathcal P_{\mathrm{triv}}$ and to $g_{[1]}:\mathcal O_{[1]}\to\mathcal P_{[1]}$. Restricting along $g_{\mathrm{triv}}$ and then to the $[1]$-fiber is the same simplicial map as restricting to $\mathcal P_{[1]}$ and then along $g_{[1]}$, on every parameter simplex, so $E_{\mathcal O}g_{\mathrm{triv}}^*=g_{[1]}^*E_{\mathcal P}$ strictly.

proof.text: Use the Cartesian algebra fibration of [lem-coef-operadic-algebra-presentability] and its pullback under $\mathcal O\mapsto\mathcal O_{\mathrm{triv}}$, which is the trivial-algebra fibration of the statement. For $g:\mathcal O\to\mathcal P$, associativity of precomposition gives $g_{\mathrm{triv}}^*\tau_{\mathcal P}^*=\tau_{\mathcal O}^*g^*$ coherently. A Cartesian lift here is restriction followed by the identity transformation; hence $R=\tau^*$ preserves Cartesian edges. Steps 1 and 2 give left adjoints $L_{\mathcal O}\dashv R_{\mathcal O}$ on all fibers. These are exactly the input data for the existing relative-adjoint theorem, after taking opposites in the next step.

source.place: Lemma 3.6.7 proof; first part of old step 5.

proof.text: Under the order reversal defined in [lem-coef-infinity-relative-cone-equivalence](4), $\Lambda_n^n$ becomes $\Lambda_0^n$ and the distinguished last edge becomes the first edge. Thus the Cartesian horn and target-lift conditions of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations] become the cocartesian horn and source-lift conditions. In particular the two opposite total fibrations are cocartesian and $R^{\mathrm{op}}$ preserves cocartesian edges. The same opposite mapping-space equivalence reverses the fiber adjunction $L_{\mathcal O}\dashv R_{\mathcal O}$ to $R_{\mathcal O}^{\mathrm{op}}\dashv L_{\mathcal O}^{\mathrm{op}}$. This is a reindexing of the defining lifting diagrams and the given adjunction equivalence, with no additional existence assertion.

source.place: Lemma 3.6.7 proof; elementary opposite specialization of the relative-adjoint theorem used in old step 5.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-cocartesian-relative-right-adjoint] to $R^{\mathrm{op}}$ over $(\operatorname{Opd}^{\mathrm{ns}}_\infty)^{\mathrm{op}}$. The preceding two steps verify its cocartesian-fibration, edge-preservation and fiber-right-adjoint hypotheses. It supplies a right adjoint to $R^{\mathrm{op}}$, agreeing with the specified fiber adjunctions and with unit, counit and triangle homotopies over the identity of the opposite base. Taking opposites gives $L\dashv R$ over the original base, with $L$ fixing the operad. By the natural opposite mapping-space equivalences of [lem-coef-infinity-relative-cone-equivalence](4), the cited relative-adjoint theorem supplies the adjunction equivalence over each base mapping space and hence on the fiber over every $g:\mathcal O\to\mathcal P$, including coherent higher simplices. This is the claimed relative free adjunction.

source.place: Lemma 3.6.7 proof; Higher Algebra Proposition 7.3.2.6 via the existing cocartesian-relative-right-adjoint node. Non-elementary assembly of old step 5.

proof.text: For clarity, the relative equivalence just obtained has the asserted fiber formula. The Cartesian mapping-space property of [lem-coef-infinity-grothendieck-limits-colimits] identifies its source with $\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Alg}_{\mathcal O}}(L_{\mathcal O}B,g^*C)$. The fiber adjunction of step 1 identifies this with $\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Alg}_{\mathcal O_{\mathrm{triv}}}}(B,\tau_{\mathcal O}^*g^*C)$. Substitute the coherent identity $\tau_{\mathcal O}^*g^*=g_{\mathrm{triv}}^*\tau_{\mathcal P}^*$ from step 4 and apply the same Cartesian mapping-space property in the trivial-algebra fibration. The result is $\operatorname{Map}_{/g}(B,\tau_{\mathcal P}^*C)$. Each arrow is the unit-induced map of the relative adjunction from step 6, and the equivalence there is over the full base mapping space, so its restrictions are natural in $g$ and all higher homotopies.
